findings_addressed.oracle: Exact integer progression 0 -> 1 -> 2: each direct call to invoke_refresh_threads() must increment refresh_call_count by exactly 1. The expected values are derived from the counting semantics of the override body, not from any injected data.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In _CountingThreadsTab._refresh_threads (test file), change `self.refresh_call_count += 1` to `self.refresh_call_count += 0` (no-op); the assertions `== 1` and `== 2` both fail immediately.

findings_addressed.oracle: The expected TID list [1001, 1002, 1003] is constructed independently as a Python literal before calling update_thread_list; the actual combo userData values are then compared with == against that literal. The oracle path (building expected_tids) is entirely separate from the production code path (ThreadsTab.update_thread_list -> QComboBox.addItem).
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In ThreadsTab.update_thread_list (src/intellicrack/ui/panels/process_panel/threads_tab.py, line 109), change `combo.addItem(f"TID {t.tid}", t.tid)` to `combo.addItem(f"TID {t.tid}", 0)`; _combo_tids returns [0, 0, 0] instead of [1001, 1002, 1003] and the == assertion fails.

notes: Both findings were tautological pre-state assertions (checking initial zero/empty state before any operation). They were hardened into before->after transition tests: G0057 now drives two direct calls and asserts exact count progression 0->1->2; G0058 now drives update_thread_list with a known 3-TID batch and asserts all five combos contain exactly those TIDs in order. A public invoke_refresh_threads() wrapper was added to _CountingThreadsTab to avoid reportPrivateUsage violations from basedpyright.
